correctness.rationale: The Euler kernel at [v] is (V/⟨v⟩)*, so the bivector contraction on its second exterior power is nonzero: vanishing would force ω∈v∧V, of rank at most two. The kernel is locally free of rank nine and agrees with the restricted-hyperplane kernel in the Euler–Koszul sequence. Splitting V=H⊕M splits the restricted Euler kernel into Ω¹_Π(1) and M*⊗O, giving O⊕Ω¹_Π(2)^3⊕O(1)^3 after exterior square and twist. The map on the last three summands is evaluation on the image ω̄ in ∧²(V/H). If nonzero, one O(1) maps isomorphically onto the target; subtracting the other components using this section gives the stated kernel. If ω̄=0, the annihilator of H is isotropic under ω, equivalently H is Lagrangian under the inverse form. In dual Lagrangian complements ω has only mixed terms, so the map is then a surjection from Ω¹_Π(2)^3 and the other summands are in the kernel. The Euler sequence gives h⁰(Ω¹_Π(1))=0; the two kernels therefore have h⁰ after twisting by −1 equal to 2 and 3. In a graph chart of Gr(3,V) around a Lagrangian plane, write ω as a sum of wedges of dual complementary basis vectors. A graph map H→H* sends the projected H vectors to negatives of their images, so the differential of ω̄ is the surjective alternating-part map to ∧²H*. This gives the regular reduced six-dimensional zero locus, without identifying a separately defined Fitting scheme. The argument is replayable from RESULT.md lines 27–53. The coordinate checker was inspected, not run; its printed Chern and cohomology summaries are not independent computations of the plane restrictions. For example c₁(Ω¹_Π(2))=1 and c₁(K_H)=2 directly, giving c₁=5 for both restrictions.

evidence: Existing bundle constructions provide the contraction or quotient input. The new computation detects its component on ∧²(V/H) and analyzes its kernel both where that component vanishes and where it has rank one.
claim_vs_prior_implication.reasoning: Uniform line splitting does not force plane isomorphism: both plane types occur here despite that common splitting. The inspected constructions do not work out the plane component and both restriction types.

evidence: The 14-section presentation and uniform line splitting occur in the first source. The second has the symplectic bivector quotient of ∧²Q. In the notation of this record the plane problem can equivalently be posed for the dual of that quotient twisted by O(1).
equivalent_formulations.reasoning: Dualizing the quotient recovers the bundle description because Ω¹(1)=Q*. It does not identify the two plane restrictions or the jump. A statement about lying in the same open moduli subset does not itself give an isomorphism of examples.

originality.rationale: The bundle and its uniform line behavior are antecedents, not credited here. The bounded pass is for the two restrictions to all linear planes and the exact cohomology jump separating them. Distinct same-day findings on lines and twisted cubics do not supply that classification.
residual_risks: A targeted primary literature search was unavailable. The relevant cited primary passages and close catalogue records were still compared; a plane classification in uninspected work cannot be ruled out. No priority is inferred from same-day indexing.

value.rationale: Planes are the next linear test after lines for a uniform bundle. The calculation shows exactly what the line splitting misses: two distinct restriction types, detected by a cohomology jump that intrinsically picks out the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The value is in the exhaustive plane classification and its geometric locus, not the coordinate-plane checks or a claim about Fitting schemes.
